name: Accessibility Rulebook
summary: Usable by everyone, designed in from the start. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA.
check: Keyboard-only walkthrough of the main flow; screen reader pass with VoiceOver or NVDA.

rules.title: Semantic HTML first
rules.text: Landmarks (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `footer`), real headings in order, lists as lists, tables as tables, buttons as buttons. ARIA only where HTML has no element for the job.

rules.title: Language set
rules.text: `<html lang="…">`, and `lang` on passages in another language.

rules.title: Skip link
rules.text: A "Skip to content" link as the first focusable element.

rules.title: Page titles
rules.text: Each page has a unique, descriptive `<title>`; in single-page apps it updates on route change and focus moves to the new content.

rules.title: Contrast
rules.text: Text 4.5:1 (large text 3:1), UI components and focus indicators 3:1 against neighbours (`CL-09`). Placeholder and disabled text that carries information also pass.

rules.title: Visible focus
rules.text: A focus ring of at least 2 px with 3:1 contrast, never removed with `outline: none` without a replacement; use `:focus-visible`.

rules.title: Text alternatives
rules.text: Meaningful alt text on informative images, `alt=""` on decorative ones, labels on icon-only buttons (`aria-label`), captions or transcripts for video and audio.

rules.title: Zoom and reflow
rules.text: Works at 200 % zoom and at 320 px width without horizontal scrolling; users can change text spacing without breaking the layout.

rules.title: Keyboard everything
rules.text: Every interactive element reachable and usable by keyboard in a logical order, no keyboard traps, custom widgets follow the ARIA Authoring Practices keyboard patterns.

rules.title: Target size and spacing
rules.text: Touch targets at least 44 × 44 px with space between neighbours; never below the WCAG 2.2 AA floor of 24 × 24 px (`IX-05`).

rules.title: Time traps
rules.text: Time limits can be extended; carousels and auto-playing media can be paused.

rules.title: Reduced motion
rules.text: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` replaces movement with fades or instant changes but keeps the state change visible. Do not kill all transitions to 0 ms if feedback is lost.

rules.title: Flashing content
rules.text: Nothing flashes more than three times per second.

rules.title: Reduced transparency and more contrast
rules.text: Honour `prefers-reduced-transparency` (solid surfaces instead of glass) and `prefers-contrast: more` (stronger borders and text).

rules.title: Announce changes
rules.text: Loading, success and errors are announced to screen readers (`aria-live`, `role="status"`, `role="alert"`), not only shown.

rules.title: Test accessibility before every release
rules.text: Run it, do not assume it: an axe or Lighthouse accessibility audit (no serious issues, score 95+), a keyboard-only walkthrough, a screen reader pass (VoiceOver or NVDA, and VoiceOver or TalkBack on a phone) on the main flow, contrast checks and a 200 % zoom check, on desktop and on a real phone, before every handoff and release.

rules.title: Focus not obscured
rules.text: A focused element is never hidden behind sticky headers, footers, cookie bars or chat widgets (WCAG 2.2, 2.4.11).

rules.title: Alternatives to dragging
rules.text: Everything done by dragging (sliders, sorting, maps) can also be done with single clicks or taps (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.7).

rules.title: Consistent help
rules.text: Help, contact and chat links appear in the same place on every page (WCAG 2.2, 3.2.6).

rules.title: No redundant entry
rules.text: Information the user already gave in the same process is filled in or selectable, not asked again (WCAG 2.2, 3.3.7).

rules.title: Accessible sign-in
rules.text: Sign-in never requires solving a puzzle or remembering and retyping a code without help: allow paste, password managers, passkeys or email links (WCAG 2.2, 3.3.8).

rules.title: Link text that makes sense alone
rules.text: Links say where they go ("Read the delivery terms"), so a list of links read out of context still works.

rules.title: Headings describe their section
rules.text: Every heading tells what the section is about; screen reader users jump through headings like a table of contents.

rules.title: Accessibility statement
rules.text: Sites that sell to EU consumers publish an accessibility statement and a way to report barriers, as the European Accessibility Act requires since 28 June 2025.

rules.title: Positive tabindex
rules.text: Never use `tabindex` greater than 0. It breaks the natural focus order; fix the DOM order instead.

rules.title: Blocking zoom
rules.text: Never set `maximum-scale=1` or `user-scalable=no` in the viewport meta tag.

rules.title: Instructions by sense alone
rules.text: Never say "click the red button" or "see the box on the right". Refer to labels people can find in any mode.

rules.title: Accessibility overlays
rules.text: Do not install overlay widgets that promise automatic compliance. They do not fix the underlying markup and often get in the way of assistive technology.
